attachments.document_title: Employment contract or other record of the start of employment
attachments.label: A1
attachments.text:
EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT (extract)

Between
Ahornweid Management Ltd, Lausanne, represented by Ms Clara Hofer, Property Manager (the employer)
and
Mr Jack Meier, Gartenstrasse 68, Lausanne (the employee)

1. Position
The employee is engaged as a building caretaker for the residential properties managed by the employer in Lausanne.

2. Start of employment
The employment begins on 19 January 2026.

3. Working time and pay
The employee works part-time according to the weekly rota. The gross monthly wage is CHF 2,090, paid at the end of each month.

4. Duties
Cleaning of common areas, small repairs, waste collection, contact with tenants.

Lausanne, 12 January 2026

For the employer: Clara Hofer
Employee: Jack Meier

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual agreement, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract set a probation period other than the first month of employment?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Where a protected period (illness or accident, compulsory service, pregnancy or birth, as above) is raised: was the notice given before that period began, with the notice period not yet expired when it began?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Was the employee pregnant, or within sixteen weeks after giving birth, on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Was the employee performing Swiss compulsory military service, civil defence service or alternative civilian service on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running, or, for such a service lasting more than eleven days, did either of those fall within the four weeks before or after it?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Was the notice given while the probation period was still running, counting any extension of the probation period under art. 335b para. 3 (a probation period interrupted by illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation is extended accordingly)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Was the employee, through no fault of their own, wholly or partly prevented from working by illness or accident on the day notice was given or at some time while the notice period was running, and was the incapacity at that point still within its protected length: up to 30 days in the first year of service, 90 days in the second to fifth years, 180 days from the sixth year?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam

I've attached my employment contract with Ahornweid Management Ltd so you can see who I work for and when I started there.

I need advice quickly. I'm a caretaker for their buildings in Lausanne and I've had a really bad few weeks. I had to do my civil defence service, which was called up for this winter, and that service overlapped with my notice period. My colleague Owen Lüthi covered my buildings while I was away, so nobody can say the work was left undone.

On top of that I got pneumonia. My doctor wrote me off sick for ten days and I have the certificate. That sick leave overlapped with my notice period as well. I didn't choose to get ill, I caught it like half of Lausanne did this winter.

The notice itself: on 7 February 2026 Clara Hofer, the manager, gave me a letter saying they were ending my employment. She said it was 'not working out' and that was all.

I know they will say I was still on trial, and that's true, I had only started on 19 January so I was still in my trial period when she gave me the letter. But I'd like to know whether my service and my illness change anything about that notice. My wage was CHF 2,090 a month and I have rent to pay at Gartenstrasse 68.

Can you tell me what I can do and whether the dates matter here?

Thank you,
Jack Meier
